transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-01-28
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Cruz (Redwood SE), Marta Ivanov (Redwood CSM); Jorge Mendes (Nimbleframe CTO), Priya Rao (Nimbleframe Lead SRE), Lynn Ho (Nimbleframe PM), Ethan Cole (Nimbleframe Security)
Recording: [link not included]

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align on onboarding milestones, runtime readiness for Nimbleframe's chat and summarization features, initial perf benchmarks, security/compliance requirements (KMS, SSO, audit logs) and next steps to start a pilot.

Topics covered:
- Current stack + infra constraints (GCP, VPC peering)
- Expected QPS and latency SLOs
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (on-prem) tradeoffs
- Data residency and KMS/Key management preferences
- Pilot scope + success metrics

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — this is Samir from Redwood, I'm the AE on the Nimbleframe account along with Elena our SE and Marta from success. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Jorge Mendes: Jorge here, hi.
[00:08] Priya Rao: Priya on SRE.
[00:09] Lynn Ho: Lynn, product.
[00:10] Ethan Cole: Ethan, security.
[00:12] Elena Cruz: Hi all, Elena here, I'll be owning the technical runbooks and the perf testing.
[00:16] Marta Ivanov: Marta, CS lead.
[00:20] Samir Patel: Great. Goal for today is to align on timelines, requirements for the pilot, and make sure we have the right ECM — sorry, the right envs and contacts. If we cover this we can get the VPC set up and the pilot scheduled.
[00:35] Jorge Mendes: High level context: Nimbleframe is building an internal assistant for support summarization and code search augmentation, mostly GCP-hosted; we want low latency for in-product assist. We're trying to decide between Redwood hosted API for speed to market vs dedicated reserved capacity for predictable tail latencies.
[01:02] Priya Rao: Our main constraints: no PHI leaving our project, we need VPC peering and customer-managed keys ideally. We also have a 99th percentile latency target around 120 ms for small-ish prompts (200 tokens). Cost matters but latency and data controls are primary.
[01:22] Samir Patel: Totally — that's a common tradeoff. To clarify, Redwood Private (VPC) would keep inference inside your project/peering, dedicated gives predictable throughput, hosted is fastest to get started but depends on network hop. We can map the exact SLOs to the deployment option.
[01:40] Lynn Ho: Timeline wise we want a pilot by mid-March. Is that realistic?
[01:45] Elena Cruz: If we get the VPC peering and keys early, yes. The critical path is network + KMS exchange and then a perf run. Our perf run typically takes a week to instrument and two days of steady-state runs.
[02:05] Ethan Cole: For security, we'll need SOC 2 attestation, audit logs, and KMS integration that supports our HSM provider (Entrust/Tresor). Do you have a SOC attestation?
[02:18] Marta Ivanov: Yes, Redwood has SOC 2; we'll share the cert and the compliance one-pager. For KMS we support customer-managed keys via our integration, but Elena can detail the flow.
[02:31] Elena Cruz: Quick tech note — depending on model and token lengths, we suggest a quantization and batching profile. Also note our runtime does automatic KV cache and prefix caching but sometimes the docs transcribe KV as K V cash in the auto notes, ignore that.
[02:50] Priya Rao: Can you explain the KV cache effect on latency — we care about tail lat worse?
[02:57] Elena Cruz: Sure — with prefix/KV caching cold starts are heavier but repeated context is faster; continuous batching reduces per-token cost but must be balanced with latency SLOs. In Dedicated you control batch windows and max latency; for Hosted we recommend smart routing and cache-friendly prompts.
[03:20] Jorge Mendes: Another point — do you support model pinning and rollbacks? We need deterministic model versions during the pilot.
[03:27] Samir Patel: Absolutely, model version pinning and canary rollouts are in the Console. We'll share a short runbook for rollouts and pinned endpoints.
[03:36] Lynn Ho: On data residency, our legal wants logs to remain in-region. Is that possible?
[03:42] Samir Patel: Yes, we support region pinning; for Private we can ensure controls in your VPC. For Hosted we can restrict regions but you'll want Dedicated or Private to guarantee residency plus audit logs retention.
[03:58] Ethan Cole: About SSO and RBAC — we use SAML via Okta. How is access to the console and audit logs handled?
[04:05] Marta Ivanov: We have SAML SSO support and RBAC. We'll need to coordinate SCIM or SAML metadata exchange. We'll put the SSO guide in the follow-up.
[04:15] Priya Rao: Perf numbers — what baseline should we expect when you say 120 ms 99th? That seems tight, curious about the assumptions.
[04:24] Elena Cruz: That 120 ms is aggressive for many generative models at 200 tokens if you include network time. What we normally show is sub-100 ms token latency on optimized kernels for smaller models but for full-sequence completion the end-to-end 99th commonly sits higher. We should run benchmarks with your prompt set so we can be precise.
[04:48] Jorge Mendes: Ok we'll share the sample prompts and a set of real calls. Is there a privacy-preserving way to run benchmarks?
[04:55] Elena Cruz: Yes — you can anonymize or obfuscate PII; we also support running the perf harness inside your VPC in Private mode so data never leaves your network.
[05:05] Samir Patel: To help with decisions, I'll send a short matrix (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) with expected cost buckets and latency characteristics.
[05:14] Lynn Ho: Great — backups on cost, do you have guidance on tokenization differences? We use sometimes long docs, average 1k tokens per session, so we need to know memory and kv cache behavior.
[05:24] Elena Cruz: For longer sequences KV cache size and sequence length matter; our runtime selects kernels and memory layout per model. For 1k tokens you'd likely want either model variants tuned for long context or offload to quantized variants to stay within GPU memory. We can recommend quant profiles after we see sample workloads.
[05:47] Priya Rao: Any concerns about multi-tenant data leakage on shared hosted?
[05:52] Samir Patel: For Hosted API we have strict isolation at request level and logging controls, but customers with strict compliance usually prefer Dedicated or Private. We'll map options.
[06:05] Jorge Mendes: On the pilot success metrics — we propose: 1) 99th latency under 250 ms for average prompt (initial), 2) 95% of calls within cost target X, and 3) no data leaves region and KMS integration validated. Thoughts?
[06:21] Marta Ivanov: Those are reasonable starting success criteria. We'll help refine them during the perf run.
[06:29] Samir Patel: Next steps recap — we'll share the VPC checklist, SAML doc, SOC2, and pricing matrix. Elena will propose perf test dates. Customer to share prompts and qps numbers.
[06:42] Lynn Ho: Who's point for the perf run?
[06:45] Elena Cruz: I'll own it with Priya as contact.
[06:48] Priya Rao: Sounds good.
[06:50] Ethan Cole: Quick question re: KMS — do you support wrapping keys with a customer HSM like YubiHSM?
[06:57] Elena Cruz: We integrate with major cloud KMS providers and have HSM-compatible flows; for specialized HSMs we usually do a short security design call. I'll flag that as an action.
[07:10] Jorge Mendes: Any blockers on your side for mid-March pilot?
[07:14] Samir Patel: Nothing blocking; depends mainly on network and keys. If we get those in next two weeks we can hit mid-March.
[07:22] Lynn Ho: Ok we'll aim to provide required artifacts by Feb 7th.
[07:28] Samir Patel: Perfect. A couple of small notes — sometimes our auto-transcript system mis-hears model names, so if you see weird names in notes ignore them (example: Redwood Dedicated sometimes comes out 'Redwoo Dedi' in auto text).
[07:42] Marta Ivanov: We'll share the onboarding playbook and schedule weekly 30-min standups during the pilot.
[07:49] Jorge Mendes: Thanks all.
[07:51] Samir Patel: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and action items.
[07:55] Elena Cruz: Bye.

End of meeting.

Artifacts referenced:
- VPC deployment checklist (link to be provided)
